newsitem.title: BURMA: Burma dismisses EU move to cut trade privileges.
newsitem.headline: Burma dismisses EU move to cut trade privileges.

text.p: Burma on Thursday dismissed a decision by the European Union (EU) to stop giving Burma concessional trade privileges, saying the move would not hurt its economy.

Burmese official newspapers said: "They would think Myanmars (Burmese) would become bewildered and wide-eyed and come kneeling down and be subservient. However, Myanmar felt nothing about it and did not care less and even did not blink eyes."
The EU on March 24 stripped Burma of special trading privileges in reaction to reports that it had used forced labour to help boost exports.
The decision would deprive Burma of generalised system of preferences (GSP) benefits that it had received for exporting agricultural and industrial products to the EU.
EU-Burmese trade amounted to 41 million European currency units ($47.2 million) a year, about a quarter of which enjoyed lucrative GSP tariff breaks.
Stressing Burma's self-reliance, the commentary said the country had undertaken by itself many road, bridge, dam, power station and factory projects without foreign assistance.
"There was no one to lend a helping hand. They were built with own strength. There is no one to thank about," it said.
An analyst said the loss of the GSP status might affect foreign investment in Burma, especially in the export-oriented garment industry.
